newsitem.title: USA: Yellow Freight to make operation changes.
newsitem.headline: Yellow Freight to make operation changes.

text.p: Yellow Freight Systems, a division of Yellow Corp, said Friday it has contacted the International Brotherhood of Teamsters with a plan for operational changes.

Yellow Freight said about 1,000 employees who are union members will be offered new jobs in other locations because of the plan, and the offers include a relocation benefit. No layoffs are included in the plan, Yellow said.

Under the changes, the company will strive to use more rail services and trucks with sleeper compartments and operated by two-person teams, which allow for continual operation. The company said the plan improves flexibility and cuts costs.

Under the four-year Teamster contract, the company said it is permitted to use 28 percent of rail service to supplement truck services. The plan calls for 26.5 percent rail, compared with about 18 percent in 1996, Yellow said.
Yellow is allowed to make changes twice during the four-year contract, and this will be the second time, the company said.
A hearing on the changes is scheduled for the week of March 3, and implementation is expected on April 13.
